review_candidates.description: The Nuclear Company is the fastest growing AI tech-enabled startup in the nuclear and energy space, pioneering a fleet-scale approach to building the next generation of nuclear reactors. Through our design-once, build-many model, we're accelerating the deployment of safe, reliable, and affordable nuclear energy. We operate with an AI-first mindset. Every employee is expected to leverage AI, technology, and the Nuclear Operating System (NOS) as integral components of their role to improve the quality, speed, and impact of their work. We expect every team member to continuously identify opportunities to automate workflows, enhance decision-making, improve processes, and contribute to the ongoing evolution of NOS as a strategic operating capability that enables The Nuclear Company to scale with excellence. They are not words on a wall; they are the standard by which we operate. TRUST is the foundation of our safety culture, fostering intellectual honesty, accountability, and open communication, while our values challenge every team member to execute with urgency, humility, resilience, and an unwavering commitment to our mission. About The Role The Nuclear Company is seeking a Senior Systems Administrator to securely administer and scale Microsoft 365, Microsoft Entra ID, managed endpoints, AWS, and Windows/Linux server environments. This role serves as the primary administrator and Tier 3 escalation point for assigned platforms, remediates legacy configuration risks, and builds automation that makes provisioning, compliance evidence, and reporting repeatable. The Senior Systems Administrator partners with Infrastructure, Cybersecurity, HR, Legal, and Engineering to maintain reliable, auditable services and support the organization's compliance and audit-readiness objectives. The ideal candidate is a hands-on technical professional with a security-first mindset who moves effectively in a fast-paced environment and automates high-value, repeatable work. Responsibilities Microsoft 365 and Identity Administration Administer and securely scale Microsoft 365, including Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, mail flow, retention, sharing, and licensing. Administer Microsoft Entra ID, SSO, MFA, Conditional Access, role-based access control, privileged access, and user lifecycle processes. Audit user and administrator accounts, security groups, roles, and licenses; remediate orphaned identities, excessive access, and legacy configuration issues. Configure and operate assigned DLP and insider-risk technical controls in partnership with Cybersecurity and Legal and in accordance with approved policies and applicable requirements. Endpoint and Device Lifecycle Management Standardize enrollment and compliance through Intune across Windows, macOS, and iOS, and use NinjaOne or another approved RMM platform for supported endpoint monitoring and management. Maintain device naming, security baselines, configuration policies, patching, software deployment, inventory accuracy, and remediation workflows. Support the complete device lifecycle, including onboarding, refresh, reassignment, and secure offboarding. Cloud and Server Administration Administer and maintain Microsoft Azure and AWS environments, with Azure serving as a primary enterprise platform. Establish scalable standards across both platforms for identity and access management, security configuration, logging, monitoring, backup, and recovery to support current operations and future growth. Administer Windows Server and Linux environments, including Active Directory, Group Policy, DNS, DHCP, system hardening, patching, and operational monitoring. Maintain system backup and recovery procedures, perform documented restoration tests, and support execution of disaster recovery plans owned by the Manager, Infrastructure & Operations. Automation and Process Improvement Build PowerShell automation, supplemented by Bash or Python where appropriate, for provisioning, compliance validation, reporting, and routine administration. Develop repeatable, scalable processes for system deployment, configuration management, and lifecycle administration. Use approved AI-assisted tools responsibly to improve scripting, troubleshooting, documentation, and operational reliability. Maintain current procedures, system documentation, runbooks, and evidence needed for operational continuity and audits. Tier 3 Escalation and Cross-Functional Support Serve as the Tier 3 escalation point for complex Microsoft 365, identity, endpoint, AWS, and server issues within the role's assigned scope. Lead multi-system troubleshooting and coordinate handoffs to Infrastructure, Network, Cybersecurity, application owners, or vendors when issues cross ownership boundaries. Partner with HR, Legal, Engineering, and other business functions on onboarding, offboarding, access, automation, and audit-readiness initiatives. Provide technical guidance and reusable troubleshooting documentation to IT Support Specialists. Experience Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience, plus at least 5 years of progressive systems administration experience. Strong Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Entra ID administration experience, including Exchange Online, SharePoint Online, Conditional Access, security groups, RBAC, licensing, and identity lifecycle management. Hands-on endpoint and server administration experience using Intune across Windows, macOS, and iOS; Windows Server, Active Directory, and Group Policy; and familiarity with RMM concepts. Advanced PowerShell automation skills, a solid command of networking fundamentals (TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, and VLANs), and a disciplined troubleshooting approach for complex, multi-system issues; ability to use approved AI-assisted tools responsibly in technical workflows. Preferred Experience Experience with zero-trust architecture, privileged identity management, or Microsoft Purview information-protection capabilities. Experience in a regulated or high-assurance environment such as nuclear, energy, defense, or the federal sector. Familiarity with frameworks and requirements such as NIST SP 800-53, CMMC, NRC cybersecurity guidance, or 10 CFR 73.54. Familiarity with automation or configuration-management tools beyond PowerShell, such as Bash, Python, Terraform, or Ansible Experience with NinjaOne or a comparable RMM platform; knowledge of ITIL or similar service-management practices; and experience with observability or AIOps platforms. review_candidates.title: Infrastructure Engineer
review_candidates.description: Infrastructure Engineer BSS Location: Hybrid; with regular travel expected to client site or Logiq’s offices in Bristol, Chippenham or Exeter. Salary: Negotiable, plus up to 10% performance bonus*, plus excellent benefits package. Logiq is a fast-growing Technology Company, providing cutting-edge solutions to high-risk clients across Private and Public Sector. Due to rapid growth in our Architecture Capability, we are looking for experienced Solution or Technical Architecture Consultants to join our team. Bespoke Secure Solutions (BSS) is part of the Architecture Practice which brings together highly experienced technologists and IT professionals with a passion for delivering complex solutions that drive tangible uplifts in capability for clients and their users. We specialise in Enterprise and Solution Architecture, Systems Engineering, Service Management and DevOps, to build highly effective teams tailored to the problem-space and requirements. As part of the BSS Team , you’ll have the opportunity to: Develop solutions for complex and unique operating environments Adapt leading edge technology solutions for novel and challenging use cases Build effective multi-discipline teams capable of delivering to the highest assurance levels We thrive on the collaborative success of highly skilled engineering teams that deliver impactful change, supporting our clients to make a difference and achieve their mission. Why Join Us? Work on impactful projects that unlock value from the latest technology and innovation. Join a practice of enthusiastic IT professionals, always willing to learn, share and collaborate Access professional development pathways tailored to your career ambitions. Enjoy flexible working arrangements and a competitive benefits package. The Role: The IT Infrastructure Engineer is a suitably qualified and experienced person (SQEP) responsible for the detailed design, build, testing, and delivery of system components within the scope of their responsibility. This scope, along with relevant Requirements will be provided by the Lead Solution Architect. Fulfilment criteria, along with testing evidence required, will be agreed with the Lead Solution Architect, Systems Engineer, Service Architect and Lead Security Architect. They will work in close collaboration with the Lead Solution Architect and other delivery and service stakeholders. Key Responsibilities Design & Build Design infrastructure solutions (hardware, software, network, platform) that meet functional and non-functional requirements defined by the Lead Solution Architect. Build and configure infrastructure components in accordance with agreed design standards and security/compliance requirements. Document the solution using a range of methods that include key design decisions, architectural rationale and build & configuration artefacts in order to deliver a Low-Level Design (LLD). Integration with other relevant subsystems and components across the technical solution. Security In collaboration with the Lead Security Architect and Lead Solution Architect, define security control implementation based upon the risk assessment and control recommendations. Service Management In collaboration with the Service Architect, determine, document and undertake the transition for the as-is to the to-be solution within their scope of responsibility and create relevant service artefacts as agreed with the Service Architect and Lead Solution Architect. Testing In collaboration with the Systems Engineer, define and undertake testing to demonstrate fulfilment of requirements including Functional, Service, Security, Performance, reliability and availability requirements. Support User Acceptance Testing as needed. It should be noted that a Low-Level Design (LLD) is considered a detailed 'design and configuration' artefact that enables the build of a solution component and assists other suitably qualified and experienced persons (SQEP) familiar with the relevant technology to understand what the function of a component is, how it has been built and what is its configuration. It should provide suitable context to the SQEP reader on key design decisions made during the design. It can take several forms including: A textual document that details the design intention and configuration in a narrative form; a script or computer code that creates the required solution component. A solution component creation method via other automated means including the use of Computer Aided Design, model-based instantiations or Artificial Intelligence which may result in a non-human readable delivery artefact, or one where specialist skills or tools are needed to interpret the artefact. A pre-configured solution component provided by a third-party with relevant installation instructions including 'appliances'; artefacts reused or repurposed from other appropriate sources. Stakeholder Engagement Collaborate with: Project Management to define deliverables and delivery timescales, assist in planning activities, manage Risk, Assumptions, Issues and Dependencies and Opportunities and support Change activities as required. Lead Solution Architect to identify scope of responsibility, relevant requirements and detailed deliverables and to ensure solution alignment with system-level architecture and programme requirements. Systems Engineer to define testable acceptance criteria for infrastructure components. Service Architect to ensure designed solutions are supportable, align with service management principles (e.g. ITIL) and create service artefacts including knowledgebase articles and operation guides as needed. Lead Security Architect to ensure that the security controls derived from the system risk assessment are agreed, included in the component design and build, well defined and testable. Delivery Support Define and maintain the Bill of Materials (BoM) for infrastructure components within their scope of responsibility, including hardware, software licenses, and support requirements. Create low-level design documentation detailing component configuration, interdependencies, and deployment. Produce operational handover documentation for the service organisation. Skills & Experience Required Proven experience in IT infrastructure engineering (e.g. compute, storage, networking, cloud, virtualisation). Experience of infrastructure delivery projects which are unconnected to corporate systems or the internet. Strong understanding of security controls and system hardening approaches for secure system delivery. Demonstrable ability to deliver infrastructure solutions in complex, multi-stakeholder environments. Strong understanding of system and service management practices and tooling. Experience producing clear, structured, and technically accurate design documentation. Knowledge of testing approaches and test planning from an infrastructure perspective. Desirable Familiarity with security frameworks and compliance standards, notably NIST (SP)800-53, CIS benchmarking and STIGs. Exposure to enterprise architecture and service transition processes. Scope of technical delivery The Project will require expertise across its delivery team in the following technologies: Management of physical hardware incl. Intel Servers, storage systems, network routers, firewalls and switches, backup devices. Networks – traditional (switches, routers, VLANs) and SDN (NSX), 802.1x. Server and Storage Virtualisation (VMware vSphere / VCF & vSAN). Windows Server Build and Role configuration (e.g., AD, file services, Network Policy (RADIUS) server, Application Server) . Windows client Build and Configuration (Windows 11, MECM). Active Directory Domain Services and 2 factor authentication . Windows-based PKI. Endpoint security software including Microsoft Defender and Trellix / McAfee Microsoft SCCM / MECM and WSUS for Windows Image deliver, software delivery and patching. System Monitoring using SCOM. Boldon James File Classifier. Databases – Oracle (for customer apps) , MS SQL Server (for MECM / SCOM). Backup and Recovery using EMC Data Domain, Tape Vaults and Dell Networker / VEEAM backup and restore software. Power Management using UPS and PowerChute software. Transition Design (migrating from the as-is system to the new system). Other information: Logiq is committed to investing in people, offering clear progression pathway into our consultancy service, and we will passionately support professional growth to develop our employees. Flexible working is available including part-time / term time working patterns. All suggestions are welcomed to be discussed as part of a proposed employment package. We are an equal-opportunities employer. *Bonus payments are discretionary and awarded upon successful completion of probation. Benefits Include: Competitive Car Allowance 10% Discretionary Very competitive Pension Scheme Access EV Scheme Access to Private Health Care Flexible Working Hybrid Working Fantastic Company Culture 10 days additional paid leave for reservists and CFAV

(Quantum) provides our national defense and federal civilian and industry customers with services and products in the following main areas: 1) Cybersecurity and Information Operations; 2) Space Operations and Control; 3) Aviation Systems; 4) Ground, Air and Missile Defense, and Fires Support Systems; 5) Intelligence Programs Support; 6) Experimentation and Test; 7) Program Management; and (8) Audio/Visual Technology Applications. Quantum's Corporate Office is located in Huntsville, AL, but Quantum actively hires for positions nationwide and internationally. We pride ourselves on providing high quality support to the U.S. Government and our Nation's Warfighters. In addition to our corporate office, we have physical locations in Colorado Springs, CO; Crestview, FL; Orlando , FL and Tupelo, MS. Mission Quantum is seeking an experienced Network Administrator to join our team in a Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility (SCIF) environment. This role involves managing and maintaining virtual and physical IT infrastructure while ensuring compliance with stringent DoD cybersecurity policies and standards. Responsibilities Manage, configure, and maintain network infrastructure in compliance with DoD cybersecurity requirements and SCIF operating standards. Configure, administer, and troubleshoot routers, switches, firewalls, VPNs, and other network infrastructure devices. Monitor network availability, performance, capacity, and security to ensure reliable and continuous operations. Collaborate with the Cybersecurity Team to implement DISA STIG requirements, remediate vulnerabilities, and maintain network security compliance. Configure and maintain network services and protocols including TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, VLANs, routing, switching, NAT, and access control lists (ACLs). Diagnose and resolve network connectivity, latency, routing, switching, and performance issues across classified and unclassified environments. Administer network authentication and access controls, including Active Directory integration, RADIUS, 802.1X, PKI, and role-based access. Configure and maintain firewalls, security policies, network segmentation, and boundary protection controls in accordance with DoD security requirements. Support network vulnerability assessments, ACAS scans, patching, configuration management, and remediation activities. Maintain network device configurations, firmware, software updates, backups, and recovery procedures. Support implementation and maintenance of secure remote-access and site-to-site VPN solutions. Perform network traffic and packet analysis using tools such as Wireshark to identify and troubleshoot network and application communication issues. Support network infrastructure modernization, lifecycle replacement, and implementation of new network technologies. Develop and maintain network diagrams, configuration baselines, standard operating procedures (SOPs), troubleshooting guides, and other technical documentation. Support RMF, ATO, inspection, audit, and continuous-monitoring activities by providing required network configuration and security evidence. Coordinate with system administrators, cybersecurity personnel, DevSecOps engineers, and external network providers to resolve infrastructure and connectivity issues. Respond to network outages and incidents, perform root-cause analysis, and implement corrective actions to minimize operational impact. Must have and maintain an appropriate DoDI 8570.01-M (Information Assurance Workforce Improvement Program) certification for the appointed duty level Solid understanding of TCP/IP networking (subnetting, routing, switching, DNS/DHCP, common protocols). Hands-on experience managing multiple Palo Alto firewalls — security rules, policies, and zones. Experience configuring and troubleshooting Cisco Catalyst 3850/9300 switches. Experience with Cisco 4311 (ISR) routers. Ability to apply STIGs to network devices and maintain compliance baselines. Hyper-V networking: virtual switches, VLAN tagging, and virtual network adapters. Experience upgrading Palo/Cisco devices Work with other teams to assist and troubleshoot network related issues. Familiarity with networking packet capture tools Familiarity with standard TCP/UDP ports Creating and maintaining network diagrams and documentation. Desired Skills And Qualifications Understanding of - Analytics and providing findings in presentation. AWS networking: VPCs, subnets, route tables, security groups, NACLs, Transit Gateway, and VPN. Terraform / Infrastructure as Code Familiarity with DoD/government compliance processes (audits, hardening, remediation, CTOs). Experience with DNS manager. We recognize the multifaceted nature of this role and value both proven experience and a genuine commitment to professional growth. Strategic Stakeholder Management: Translate complex technical strategies into clear business impacts for senior leadership and customers. You will advocate for the team’s technical strategy and facilitate open dialogue between cross functional teams and external suppliers. Innovation Champion: Proactively identify project risks and technical debt, driving timely resolution and implementing continuous improvements in engineering processes, Network and Cybersecurity standards, quality, and best practices. Decision Making: Operate with autonomy. You are empowered to make high-stakes technical decisions and pull in specialized experts when necessary to ensure successful delivery. Build functional infrastructure from the ground up (Networking, virtualization, server OS). Compliance and Lifecycle: Ensure adherence to Secure Deployment Guides and Security Assurance Plans. Manage vulnerability monitoring, patch management and disaster recovery processes. Technical Oversight: Define IP address strategies, perform substation level hardening, and evaluate Network and Cybersecurity solutions from 3rd party suppliers. Tendering and Regulatory Support: Support bidding processes with knowledge of regulations such as EU NIS, NERC, and BDES; map requirements between varying Network and Cybersecurity standards. Operational Execution: Lead design, configuration, and testing to meet project budgets and schedules. Oversee FAT (Factory Acceptance Testing) and assist with on-site installation and commissioning of LAN networks.
